text:
anya: FYI — big customer asked for a 'surge shaping' feature to throttle and isolate noisy tenants during major product launches. They want predictable p99 latency under 10s when traffic spikes. Can we sketch a decision checklist?

sam: high level ask noted. do we mean per-tenant rate shaping + capacity reservations, or more of routing-level backpressure?

anya: both. they want soft guarantees (reserved slices) + automatic shaping when others surge. core ask is to avoid noisy neighbor impact on latency/cost.

alex: quick thought — 2 levers: 1) slice reservations (reserved GPU shares) 2) dynamic traffic shaping + drop policies (fallback to cheaper model). each has tradeoffs on utilization.

maria: agree. spec should include: acceptance criteria, operator controls, telemetry (per-tenant tail latency + cost delta), and rollback gates.

patrick: also need to decide routing boundary: edge-level (region) vs fleet-level (model pool). shape at edge is cheaper but harder to enforce globally.

devops-bot: perf test scheduled: bench --rps 200 --seq 512 --tenants 50 (ETA 2h) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: propose a minimal MVP checklist to decide scope for Q2: 
- customer acceptance criteria (p99 latency target, % of requests served from reserved pool)
- feature: tenant reservations + soft preemption policy
- telemetry: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, cost per token delta, eviction events log
- rollout plan: canary with 1 big customer, 2 small customers, auto-fallback to hosted tier
- rollback: immediate disable reservations + global shaping off

anya: + add contract language with sales (SLA caveat for shaped traffic). and explicit KMS/audit requirements for private deployments.

alex: tradeoffs: reservations -> predictable latency but reduces overall GPU utilization; shaping -> better utilization but can lead to rejects. We should quantify: run bench with reserved slices at 20%/50%/80% and measure p99.

maria: migration path idea: 1) implement soft reservations (logical weight in scheduler), 2) expose tenant controls in Console (reserve X RUs), 3) add hard isolation lanes if customer opts in (Dedicated).

sam: decision needed today on scope for Q2 MVP. options: A) soft reservations + basic shaping + telemetry (safer, less infra) B) full hard isolation lanes + SLA (larger infra + sales).

anya: I'm leaning A for Q2. want engineering to deliver observable, reversible controls first.

patrick: +1 for A. but include explicit perf budget for adding hard lanes (costed tickets).

alex: i'll run the three bench permutations and post numbers. if soft reservations meets p99 <= 10s at 50% reserved we call it success threshold.

maria: operational gating checklist for canary: 
- perf: p99 under threshold for both reserved and non-reserved tenants
- telemetry: alerts for eviction >1% of requests
- runbook: how to disable/resume shaping, contact playbook for customer pain
- circuits: fallback to cheaper model or queueing policy

sam: owners: eng-platform (alex) to prototype, eng-runtime (maria) for scheduler + telemetry, product (sam/anya) for acceptance & sales contracts. timeline: prototype in 4 weeks, canary in 8.

anya: thanks. action items: alex upload bench results + csv, maria draft scheduler design doc, sam/anya draft SLA caveat + sales note. I'll coordinate with customer on pilot window. :thumbsup:

patrick: small nit — add region considerations: shaping needs to be region-aware to avoid cross-region failovers creating new surges.

alex: noted. will include region tags in bench and scheduler prototype.

sam: ok locking scope = MVP A. will create GH epic and link to this thread.

anya: great — follow-ups in #product-roadmap and I'll ping here with customer pilot dates.

patrick: thanks everyone.
